The January and February 2013 Treasurer's Reports from Assistant Superintendent Mark S. Rajter show total disbursements in period of $5,574,919.47 and $4,963,865.33. ## Meeting

Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 p.m., April 9, 2013, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public comment is limited to one-half hour each for agenda and non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

## Recognition

Spirit of Diversity Awards, in their first year and designed by the Troy Diversity Council, honor sixteen groups and individuals including Padma Kuppa, Rouba Samman, Jen Hilzinger, Nadeen Brown, Tonia Romancheck, the Troy African American Parent Network, Bemis Cultural Coffee, Jesse Allgeier, and the Troy High head peer mediators led by teacher Gail Yax. Ten teachers were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher program; Laurie Pickell (Martell) was named district Teacher of the Year and receives a free one-year car lease donated by the Suburban Collection, with Patrick Koneval (Smith) and Omar Hakim (International Academy East) also sent to Oakland Schools. The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, led by president Al Robinson, funded 114 mini-grants, a record for a single year. Jason Brolus presents Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union cash grants.

## Minutes on the consent agenda

The February 5, 2013 meeting adopted Resolutions 13-018 through 13-025, each 7-0: new hires; a two-year probationary administrative contract for Mark Washington as Director of Technology effective February 11, 2013; closing Athens and Troy High to open enrollment for 2013/2014 except not more than 25 ninth graders; authorization to prepare an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds; a 2012/2013 budget amendment; a $44,768.00 web filter award to Phantom Technologies; and second reading of policy K-1303. The March 19 special meeting adopted Resolution 13-026 for closed session on negotiations, 7-0.

February year-to-date General Fund (101, 120, 122) revenue is budgeted at $130,493,602 against $74,548,201 actual; expenditures are budgeted at $131,488,075 against $71,494,646 actual with $37,751,301 encumbered. Fund balance runs from $23,078,581 on July 1, 2012 to a projected $22,084,108 on June 30, 2013. Debt Service Funds remain negative, $(1,859,077) to $(2,666,557).

## Reports and action items

- Elementary and middle school mathematics materials adoption, reported by math coordinator Kris Karbon; middle school teachers trialed Big Ideas Math, while the Algebra 1 - Geometry - Algebra 2 sequence will make a materials recommendation next spring.
- Fall 2012 MEAP results, reported by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment: Troy's combined-grade proficiency was 87% reading, 77% math, 57% social studies and 27% science.
- Bid 9754 for copy paper to Contract Paper Group, Inc., $57,758.40, split $38,505.60 against the 2012-13 General Fund and $19,252.80 against 2013-14.
- First readings of Board Policy G-1007, Layoff and Recall of Teachers and Administrators, and G-1008, Discipline, Demotion, or Dismissal of Teachers and Administrators.
- An April 4, 2013 memorandum from Rich Machesky recommends permanent expulsion of 11th-grade student Graham Carrington for Level III conduct violations.
- Closed session on negotiations under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 p.m. on April 9, 2013 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices are at 4400 Livernois, telephone 248.823.4000, with meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The agenda runs from the Pledge of Allegiance through recognitions, additions and deletions, public communication, the general consent agenda, personnel, curriculum, business, other, closed session and adjournment.

RECOGNITION. The Spirit of Diversity Awards, in their first year and designed by the Troy Diversity Council, honor sixteen groups and individuals: Padma Kuppa; Rouba Samman and Jen Hilzinger for the Schroeder World Tour; Nadeen Brown, president of the Troy African American Parent Network; Tonia Romancheck; TAAPN, whose leaders include Aretha Bradley, Constance Dansby, Tesha Long and Cathy Hodges and whose Saturday Excel math series and tutoring carry the motto "Look for greatness in each child and you will find it"; Jen Hilzinger for Cultural Coffee hours at Boulan Park Middle School; the Troy High head peer mediators - Nico Adamski, Nicholas Arsanos, Connor Hayden, Hope Keating, Justin Losey, Miranda Mio, Thomas O'Donovan, Alexsys Pullen, Rebecca Ress, Rachel Sacco and Eve Theoharis - led by teacher Gail Yax, a group that trains more than 300 students annually; Bemis Cultural Coffee PTO members Jeanette Tanafranca, Vicki Wind, Janice Girling, Mehrun-nisa Ahmad and Kendra Cooper; and Jesse Allgeier for more than three years on the Troy Diversity Project. Honorable mentions go to the Athens Theatre Company, Sandra LewAllen, Tom Wylie, Brian Nutting, Marlene Seltzer, M.D., and Joe Thilman of PFLAG. Ten teachers were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award Program; seven were honored - Nancy Haboush (Leonard), Elizabeth Mayne (Hamilton), Lynn Mui (Wattles), Jessica Thudium (Hamilton), Karen Muzljakovich (Morse), Faith Clay (Bemis) and Alan Gieleghem (Wattles) - and three were forwarded to Oakland Schools by a TEA selection committee: Laurie Pickell (Martell), Patrick Koneval (Smith Middle School) and Omar Hakim (International Academy East). Pickell was also named the district's Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year lease of a car donated by the Suburban Collection. The Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, whose president Al Robinson speaks while Karen Rockwell rolls recipients on screen, funded 114 grants this year, a record number in a single year. Jason Brolus of Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union, which sponsored a pre-meeting reception, presents cash grant awards.

MINUTES. The February 5, 2013 regular meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, Superintendent Fowler and administrators Keeling, Lesser, Machesky, Rajter and Witt attending, and roughly 22 audience members. Resolution 13-018 approved the consent agenda; 13-019 hired Zachary MacIntosh, Letitia Mason, Megan Sulewski and Leah Vohs; 13-020 gave Mark Washington a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Technology effective February 11, 2013; 13-021 closed Athens High and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2013/2014 except for not more than 25 ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area, with Dr. Machesky noting the option's fourth year and consistent uptake of 22 to 23 students; 13-022 authorized preparation of an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds under the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, certified by Secretary Paula Fleming under Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976; 13-023 amended the 2012/2013 appropriations to $131,488,075 General Fund, $8,805,399 Special Revenue, $18,113,148 Debt Service, $290,713 Capital Projects and $25,000 Internal Service; 13-024 awarded the web filter bid to Phantom Technologies for $44,768.00; and 13-025 approved changes to policy K-1303, Commercial Advertising. All votes were 7-0. Enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants were presented at three levels. Elliot Gould announced Troy Youth Assistance's "Dollars for Education" 50/50 raffle, $25 per ticket with only 2,000 sold and a drawing April 25. Student representatives Patty Durell (Troy High), Aishawarya Singh (Athens, Charity Week goal $28,000 for Angels of Hope) and Miranda Wilson (Niles) reported; the meeting adjourned at 7:53 p.m. The February 12 workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 10:40 p.m.; the March 19 workshop ran 6:10 p.m. to 7:43 p.m. with Mr. Schmidt participating by remote communications; the March 19 special meeting adopted Resolution 13-026 to enter closed session on negotiations by roll call, 7-0, at 7:54 p.m., adjourning at 9:20 p.m.

TREASURER'S REPORTS. Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, certifies both months. January 2013 disbursements by fund: General Fund $2,484,262.24, Grant $11,067.64, Special Education $182,765.78, Food Service $11,104.81, Troy Career Center $19,726.60, Community Education $18,413.49, Debt Funds (304, 306, 312) $109,765.61 and Student Activity $167,349.51. The January summary, dated February 14, 2013, shows General Fund $2,678,095.66, Special Revenue $49,244.90 and Other Funds $277,115.12 for total check disbursements of $3,004,455.68, plus ACH debits $31,513.99, outgoing wire transfers $2,146,818.77, P-Card purchases $399,452.89 and prior period voids of ($7,321.86), for total disbursements in period of $5,574,919.47. February disbursements by fund: General $2,333,941.29, Grant $12,545.00, Special Education $153,057.98, Food Service $10,311.54, Troy Career Center $21,271.88, Community Education $40,567.01, Debt Funds $16,611.06, Building & Site $1,250.00 and Student Activity $62,680.85. The February summary, dated April 2, 2013, shows General Fund $2,499,544.27, Special Revenue $72,150.43 and Other Funds $80,541.91 for total checks of $2,652,236.61, ACH debits $48,498.27, wire transfers $2,109,992.75, P-Card purchases $154,890.98 and voids of $(1,753.28), totaling $4,963,865.33.

BUDGET REPORTS. January year-to-date General Fund revenue was budgeted at $129,234,265 against $59,466,318 actual, 53.99% uncollected; expenditures $132,398,263 against $66,237,962 actual with $49,432,154 encumbered and $16,728,147 available, and fund balance moving from $20,591,023 on July 1, 2012 to $17,427,025 at June 30, 2013. February year-to-date General Fund revenue is budgeted at $130,493,602 against $74,548,201, with local sources $37,213,220 budgeted and $33,548,435 collected and state sources $80,549,791 budgeted and $36,868,333 collected; expenditures are $131,488,075 budgeted, $71,494,646 actual and $37,751,301 encumbered, leaving $22,242,128 available; fund balance runs $23,078,581 to $22,084,108. Consolidated Special Revenue Funds show revenue of $8,594,118 budgeted and $4,730,324 actual, expenditures of $8,805,399 and $4,145,205, and fund balance $2,335,433 to $2,124,152. Food Service revenue is $3,414,309 budgeted and $2,021,806 actual with no salary or benefit expenditure, balance $964,489 to $841,757; Troy Career Center budgets both revenue and expenditures at $2,709,602, balance $35,030; Adult and Community Education revenue $2,288,467 and $1,833,243, expenditures $2,417,016 and $1,516,484, balance $1,335,914 to $1,207,365; Facilities Rental collected $416 of $181,740, balance $40,000. Debt Service Funds report revenue of $17,305,668 and $15,930,981 actual against expenditures of $18,113,148 and $2,937,223, with the $13,055,000 principal redemption still unspent and fund balance $(1,859,077) to $(2,666,557). Capital Projects Fund 404 spent $242,120 of $250,560; Capital Projects Maintenance Fund 499 shows a $1,000,000 incoming transfer budget, $40,153 in capital outlay and balance rising from $500,000 to $1,459,847; the Internal Service Fund holds $25,000 with the VRIP expense unspent.

DISBURSEMENT DETAIL. Pentamation report ACCTPA21 covers checks dated 01/01/2013-01/31/2013 (run 02/04/2013, accounting period 8/13) and 02/01/2013-02/28/2013 (run 03/06/2013, period 9/13). Wire transfers include MPSERS MIP/BD/TDP of $877,218.39 and $870,144.56, MPSERS DB $846,026.52, Sodexo invoices of $292,378.68 and $266,147.54, VRIP payments of $84,336.49 in each month, and MILAF-to-Bank of America transfers of $2,500,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. P-Card statement PCRD1212 totals $399,452.89 and includes a $178,830.00 AVI charge in Fund 404; statement PCRD0113 totals $154,890.98 and includes $25,545.00 to SSI DeltaCPO and $5,925.00 to NSBA.

STUDENT DISCIPLINE. An April 4, 2013 memorandum from Rich Machesky, Ed.D., Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction, to Dr. Barbara Fowler recommends permanent expulsion of 11th-grade student Graham Carrington for Level III violations of the Rights and Responsibilities Code of Conduct, based on a letter from Troy High School principal Mark Dziatczak.

CURRICULUM. Math coordinator Kris Karbon reports on elementary and middle school mathematics materials adoption with select high school courses, organized around four domains - Common Core alignment and design, assessment and questioning, equity and differentiation, and technology and resources - with teachers transitioning to Common Core demands since 2009-2010. Twenty-seven middle school teachers piloted Big Ideas Math; precalculus reviewers were Carla Kosiorek, Matt Mitchell, Alicia Rozak and Mike Webster, AP calculus reviewers Kristina Badgley, Matt Mitchell, Margaret Slankster and Jenny Sobczynski, and computer science reviewers Joe Moceri and Josh Pudaloff; a 30-member elementary committee also served. Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, presents Fall 2012 MEAP results for grades 3 through 9. Troy's eight-year combined reading trend runs 77, 80, 77, 78, 81, 82, 84, 87 against Oakland's 76; math ends at 77 against Oakland's 56; social studies at 57 against 40; science at 27 against 21. Correlations with free or reduced price lunch eligibility are -.95 for reading (91 percent of variance), -.93 math (86), -.94 social studies (89), -.92 writing (85) and -.91 science (82). On the residual table Troy scores 0.38 reading, 1.22 math, 0.11 science, 0.94 social studies and 0.81 writing for an average of 0.69, with South Lyon at 1.38, Rochester 1.23, Hazel Park 1.14 and Pontiac -1.83.

BUSINESS AND POLICY. Bid 9754 for copy paper was advertised March 6, 2013 and opened March 27, 2013 at 1:00 p.m. at Facility Operations/Purchasing, with 10 vendors solicited and 4 responding; the tabulation dated 4/4/2013 lists AmeriSource Supply Company at $24.49 per case and $61,714.80, Contract Paper Group, Inc. at $22.92 and $57,758.40, Costco Wholesale at $23.09 and $58,186.80 and Midland Paper at $23.18 and $58,413.60, all for 2,520 cases. The suggested resolution awards Contract Paper Group, Inc. $57,758.40, of which $38,505.60 is charged to the 2012-13 General Fund and $19,252.80 to 2013-14; the responsible cabinet administrator is Mark Rajter. First readings cover Board Policy G-1007, Layoff and Recall of Teachers and Administrators, sourced to Section 380.1248 of the Revised School Code and Section 423.215(3)(k) and barring length of service or tenure status as primary factors, and G-1008, Discipline, Demotion, or Dismissal of Teachers and Administrators, which adopts the "not arbitrary or capricious" standard under MCL 38.71 through 38.191 and MCL 38.101, sourced also to MCL 423.215(3)(m); neither may be the subject of collective bargaining, and both carry adoption dates to be determined. The meeting closes with a resolution to enter closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), by roll call of Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood.
